definitions.explanation: The top of a mountain or a prominent pointed section of a mountain range.
The blunt back edge of a sword or knife, opposite the cutting edge.

examples.japanese: ⟦{雪|ゆき}→雪：00584_yuki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦かぶった→かぶる：00709_kaburu⟧{峰|みね}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{見|み}える→見える：01165_mieru⟧。
examples.english: You can see the snow-capped peaks.

examples.japanese: ⟦{朝日|あさひ}→朝日：23495_asahi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{照|て}らされた→照らす：04669_terasu⟧{峰|みね}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{美|うつく}しかった→美しい：01121_utsukushii⟧。
examples.english: The peaks lit up by the morning sun were beautiful.

examples.japanese: いくつ⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{峰|みね}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{越|こ}えて→越える：02099_koeru⟧、ようやく⟦{目的地|もくてきち}→目的地：09996_mokutekichi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧たどり{着|つ}いた。
examples.english: After crossing many peaks, we finally reached our destination.
To strike with the back of the sword.

examples.japanese: {峰|みね}{打|う}ちなら⟦{命|いのち}→命：02371_inochi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{取|と}らぬ→取る：00565_toru⟧。
examples.english: A strike with the back of the blade won't take a life.

examples.japanese: ⟦{包丁|ほうちょう}→包丁：04976_houchou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{峰|みね}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧にんにく⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{潰|つぶ}す→潰す：00410_tsubusu⟧。
examples.english: Crush the garlic with the back of the knife.

notes:
A literary and evocative word for mountain peaks, common in nature descriptions and place names. Also has a specialized meaning in swordsmanship.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {峰|みね}{打|う}ち: striking with the back of a sword (a non-lethal blow)
- ⟦{連|つら}なる→連なる：14449_tsuranaru⟧{峰|みね}: a chain of peaks; a mountain range
- {峰|みね}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{越|こ}える→越える：02099_koeru⟧: to cross a peak
- {最高峰|さいこうほう}: the highest peak; the pinnacle (also figurative)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{頂上|ちょうじょう}→頂上：03493_choujou⟧: summit, top — specifically the very top of a mountain; more commonly used for the single highest point
- ⟦{山頂|さんちょう}→山頂：09942_sanchou⟧: mountaintop — similar to ⟦{頂上|ちょうじょう}→頂上：03493_choujou⟧; emphasizes being at the top
- ⟦{尾根|おね}→尾根：19839_one⟧: ridge — the long narrow crest of a mountain range

WRITING:
Also written as {嶺|みね} in literary contexts. The character {峰|みね} appears in many Japanese surnames and place names.
